q: How does a Morbi tile exporter count truck emissions to Mundra port?
title: Morbi tiles: trucks to Mundra port
short: Multiply tonnes carried by road kilometres and by a published intensity for the truck class. For a heavy truck of 30 to 50 tonnes, the Smart Freight Centre India default is 0.0663 kg CO2e per tonne-km. If you pay the transporter, this is Scope 3.
audience: Tile exporters in the Morbi cluster trucking containers to Mundra or Kandla

p: Tonnes per trip from the lorry receipt or weighbridge slip.
Tonnes x km x the intensity for the truck class.
Transport you pay for to the port is Scope 3 category 4. If your own trucks do it, the diesel is Scope 1 instead.

example.title: Worked example: one container trip (illustrative distance and load)
example.note: Load and distance are illustrative; 0.0663 kg CO2e per tonne-km is the SFC India default for 30 to 50 tonne trucks, well to wheel.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
